posts.title_en: From Cadet to Founder: How a Military-School Student Became a Silicon Valley Real Estate Entrepreneur
posts.title_zh: 从军校学员到创业者：一个 Texas A&M 军校生如何走进硅谷地产
posts.excerpt_en: Discipline, perseverance, growth. What the Texas A&M Corps of Cadets taught me about pressure, responsibility and getting things done, and how it shaped the way I serve sellers today.
posts.excerpt_zh: 自律、坚持、成长。Texas A&M 军校教会我的，是如何在压力下承担责任、把事情做成；这也塑造了我今天服务卖家的方式。
posts.body_en:
I came to the United States to study, and I chose one of the hardest places to do it: the Corps of Cadets at Texas A&M University.

## Cadet life: discipline and grit

Early mornings, inspections, formations, and a schedule that left no room for excuses. I was one of only three Asian women in my class. That could have been a reason to feel out of place. Instead it became a reason to show up prepared, every single day.

![From cadet to graduate](img/growth-journey.webp)

## Training: teamwork and resilience

The Corps teaches you that nothing important gets done alone. You learn to carry your share, to carry someone else's when they need it, and to keep moving when you are tired. I became an honor officer and a scholarship recipient, but what I really earned was the habit of pushing things to completion under pressure.

## Graduation: a new milestone

I graduated with a degree in Economics and Finance. The ring, the gown and the photos mark the day, but the real milestone was knowing I could set a hard goal and reach it.

![Texas A&M Corps of Cadets](img/corps-of-cadets.webp)

## From the parade field to Silicon Valley

Sixteen years of studying, living and investing in the U.S. turned into judgment, execution and the ability to create opportunity. Today I co-lead Gaea Realty, I have personally run addition, remodel and rebuild projects in the Valley, and I founded SOHO Asian Fusion to create jobs for women.

When a family trusts me with the sale of their home, the Corps is still with me: prepare thoroughly, communicate honestly, and deliver the result.

## What I would tell a student today

Choose the harder path when it teaches you something you need. Find the people who will grow with you. And remember that discipline is not the opposite of kindness; it is how you keep your promises.

Integrity first. Action first. Long-term thinking.
posts.body_zh:
我来美国读书，选了一条最难的路：Texas A&M University 的 Corps of Cadets（军校学员团）。

## 军校生活：自律与韧性

清晨集合、内务检查、列队训练，日程里没有任何借口的空间。我是同届仅有的三位亚裔女性之一。这本可以成为不自在的理由，却变成了我每天都做好准备的理由。

![从军校学员到毕业生](img/growth-journey.webp)

## 训练：团队与坚持

军校教会我：重要的事没有一件是一个人完成的。你要扛起自己的那一份，在别人需要时帮他扛，在疲惫时也继续向前。我成为荣誉军官、获得奖学金，但我真正收获的，是在压力下把事情推到落地的习惯。

## 毕业：新的里程碑

我拿到了经济与金融本科学历。戒指、学位袍和照片记录了那一天，而真正的里程碑，是我知道自己可以定下一个难的目标，并且做到。

![Texas A&M 军校](img/corps-of-cadets.webp)

## 从阅兵场到硅谷

16 年在美求学、生活与投资的经历，变成了判断力、执行力与创造机会的能力。今天我是 Gaea 家易地产的联合创始人，亲自操盘硅谷住宅的加建、改建与重建项目，也创办了 SOHO Asian Fusion，为女性创造工作机会。

当一个家庭把卖房这件事托付给我，军校的那套标准依然在：充分准备，坦诚沟通，交付结果。

## 想对今天的学生说

当更难的路能教会你需要的东西，就选它。找到愿意和你一起成长的人。也请记得，自律不是温柔的反面，而是你兑现承诺的方式。

诚信为本，行动为先，长期主义。
